raw_case_text: A 46-year-old man originating from Morocco, with a medical history of end-stage renal disease secondary to type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with chills during haemodialysis (HD) sessions on January 2011. The patient was on HD since 2007, and in 2009, he was included in a prospective study to evaluate the utility of HBHA-IGRA, compared to TST for the detection of LTBI in HD patients (Dessein et al, manuscript in preparation). The QFT-G-IT was highly positive (13.58 IU/ml) as were the PPD- and HBHA-IGRAs with respectively 18,972 pg/ml and 7,287 pg/ml IFN-gamma. These results, especially the high IFN-gamma response to the latency antigen HBHA, indicated that the patient was latently infected with Mtb. During a January 2011 HD session, the patient presented with chills and fever, but no abnormalities were noted upon physical examination, except a weight loss of 4 Kg over the previous weeks. Blood cultures remained negative. A chest radiography revealed no infiltrates, cavities or calcifications. The patient denied prior exposition to Mtb, but the QFT-G-IT was still positive, with values similar to those found two years earlier (14.36 IU/ml), whereas the HBHA-IGRA had become totally negative. However, depletion of the CD4+ regulatory T cells from the PBMC, performed as described previously and based on CD25high T cell depletion by positive immunomagnetic selection, resulted in the re-appearance of a low but positive IFN-gamma response to HBHA stimulation (134 pg/ml). At that time, the IGRA values to rESAT-6 were very high (3,855 pg/ml) so that the HBHA/rESAT-6 ratio was 0.001. Since these results strongly suggested that the patient had progressed from latent Mtb infection to active TB disease, a PET Scan analysis was done demonstrating a strong metabolic captation of cervical and mediastinal lymph nodes. A jugular lymph node was surgically removed and revealed the presence of a granuloma with caseous necrosis. Anti-tuberculosis treatment was immediately initiated (Nicotibine, Rifadine, Tebrazid, Myambutol) and resulted in progressive clinical improvement. Thirty-two days later, the lymph node culture was positive for drug-sensitive Mtb.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 46-year-old male on maintenance hemodialysis presenting with fever and chills during hemodialysis sessions and recent weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, a Moroccan man on chronic maintenance hemodialysis since 2007, presented during a hemodialysis session in January 2011 with acute rigors and fever. Over the preceding weeks, he had noted an unintentional weight loss of 4 kg. He had been enrolled in a prospective latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) study in 2009, which documented positive interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs), and he now presented with symptomatic reactivation.
subjective.past_medical_history: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to type 2 diabetes mellitus, maintained on chronic hemodialysis since 2007. Born in Morocco; denied known direct exposure to active tuberculosis. Documented latent TB infection in 2009 with strongly positive QFT-G-IT (13.58 IU/mL), PPD-IGRA (18,972 pg/mL IFN-gamma), and HBHA-IGRA (7,287 pg/mL IFN-gamma).
subjective.review_of_systems: Fever, chills during dialysis, 4 kg weight loss over recent weeks. Denies cough, dyspnea, night sweats, or localizing pain.

objective.physical_examination: Patient was febrile and chilling during dialysis; physical examination was otherwise unremarkable with no peripheral adenopathy or organomegaly noted; documented 4 kg weight loss.
objective.routine_investigations: Blood cultures were repeatedly negative. Plain chest radiograph revealed no infiltrates, cavitations, or calcifications.
objective.advanced_workup: Repeat QFT-G-IT remained positive (14.36 IU/mL). Standard HBHA-IGRA was negative (<50 pg/mL); however, following positive immunomagnetic selection depletion of CD4+CD25high regulatory T cells from PBMCs, a low positive IFN-gamma response to HBHA was restored (134 pg/mL); rESAT-6 IGRA was markedly elevated (3,855 pg/mL), yielding an HBHA/rESAT-6 ratio of 0.001 indicative of active disease. 18F-FDG PET scan demonstrated intense hypermetabolic uptake in cervical and mediastinal lymph nodes. Excisional biopsy of a cervical jugular lymph node was performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Reactivation of latent tuberculosis manifesting as active cervical and mediastinal tuberculous lymphadenitis in an end-stage renal disease patient on hemodialysis.
Diagnostic confirmation: Excisional jugular lymph node biopsy demonstrated necrotizing caseating granulomas; mycobacterial culture of the lymph node yielded drug-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis at 32 days of incubation, concordant with active-TB biomarker shift (elevated rESAT-6 IGRA with suppressed HBHA response) and PET hypermetabolism.
Management and outcome: Immediately initiated on 4-drug antituberculosis chemotherapy: Nicotibine (isoniazid), Rifadine (rifampicin), Tebrazid (pyrazinamide), and Myambutol (ethambutol). Treatment resulted in rapid, progressive clinical recovery and resolution of constitutional symptoms.
